transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Atlas Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Infra), Diane Park (Security), Ben Yu (Product)
Links shared: deck - https://bit.ly/redwood-console-tracing, security pack - https://redwood.example.com/s/docs/security-pack.pdf

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer wants to understand root-cause flow for model failures and per-request debugging; they raised concerns about data residency, KMS, and prefix/KV cache visibility for private deployments. Discussed tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated for high-throughput low-latency workloads. Agreed next steps: pricing, sample traces, schedule pilot.

Topics: tracing overview; request logs export; error analysis flows; mapping trace IDs to requests; RBAC and SSO for logs; pilot/benchmark plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to ~45 mins, i'm Maya from Redwood, this is Arjun, our SE.
[00:08] Arjun: Hi all, quick agenda — tracing, error analysis, request logs, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:15] Lina: Sounds good, thanks. For context we run a mix of hosted endpoints and a few on prem-ish clusters, our big ask is debugging noisy failures in production, especially for long conversations where KV cache mismatch seems to happen.
[00:30] Samir: Ya we see occasional spikes in token latency and some 500s, not sure if it's model timeouts, infra, or request format. We want to be able to trace a user request end-to-end.
[00:43] Arjun: Cool. i'll start with the console — at top level we have per-request traces that glue together the API request, routing decision, model shard calls and the runtime KV cache events. you can search by trace id or by user request id.
[01:05] Arjun: (screen) here is a sample trace — note we surface timeline lanes for routing, kernel selection, batching windows, and kv-cache hits/misses. sometimes the transcript shows "kv cash" in the export, the ASR messes that up.
[01:23] Ben: Is it possible to map the trace back to the raw request payload? we need to join logs with our product event id.
[01:31] Arjun: Yes, we show request.headers.X-Redwood-Request-Id and you can configure to forward your own correlation id. We'll also attach the prompt prefix hash so you can correlate cache behavior.
[01:45] Lina: And for privacy — will those logs include the full prompt text? we can't ship PHI to hosted endpoints by default.
[01:53] Maya: Good call — for hosted we have redaction options, but for Private or Dedicated you can opt to keep logs in your VPC and integrate with your KMS/HSM. Diane, you had a question on encryption?
[02:05] Diane: Yeah SOC two, the usual — how are logs stored, is encryption at rest, do you rotate keys, and can we use our own KMS? Also audit logs for who accessed traces.
[02:16] Maya: We support bring-your-own-KMS for Private, rotation policies, and Audit logs with RBAC in the console. we'll send the SOC2 + encryption docs after the call. note: sometimes the doc name is "SOC two" in the transcript, the auto-captioner did that.
[02:31] Samir: For performance debugging, can we get per-shard latency histograms? we want to know if slow tokens are from kernel selection or network jitter.
[02:40] Arjun: Yep — per-model-shard timings are logged and you can break down by kernel type. you'll see when the runtime selects a quantized path vs fp16. the console highlights hot segments and shows continuous batching windows where latency vs throughput tradeoffs happen.
[03:05] Arjun: I'll demo an error analysis flow — we have a "Request Logs" tab where you can filter by status code, model id, or a custom tag. clicking a log entry opens the linked trace with timestamps every ~15-30s in the trace timeline panel.
[03:22] (screen share)
[03:28] Arjun: here's an example 500 — you can see the stack: routing -> model shard request -> kernel OOM -> fallback model invocation. we also show the fallback policy that triggered, so you can see the canary vs stable comparison.
[03:42] Lina: That's helpful. can the console show a diff between responses when fallback happened? like compare tokens side-by-side?
[03:49] Arjun: Yes, we surface response diffs and a quality delta so you can quickly see if fallback reduced perplexity or changed safety classification. it's part of the error analysis pane.
[04:05] Ben: How easy is it to export logs to our SIEM? we use Splunk.
[04:11] Arjun: We have exporters — you can push structured request logs (JSONL) directly to your S3 or forward to Splunk/Datadog via our webhook or a connector. there may be a small lag for large exports but it's configurable.
[04:25] Samir: Any rate limits on logs export? if we do full trace exports for a pilot we'll likely need high throughput.
[04:33] Maya: For Dedicated we can enable higher export throughput; for hosted there are quotas. We'll include recommended export configs in the sizing doc we send.
[04:45] Lina: We also want more observability into caching — our hypothesis is repeated prefix misses causing repeated context rebuilds. can we get a cache-hit matrix per prefix?
[04:56] Arjun: We emit prefix-level metrics and a cache heatmap. you can query by prefix hash or user id. note: the prefix hashing algorithm is documented in the runbook — i'll share that runbook after the call.
[05:12] (minor crosstalk)
[05:16] Diane: For compliance, if we do Private deployment, do traces leave our VPC? we need guarantee they do not.
[05:23] Maya: In Private deploy, control plane can be on Redwood but logs/data plane stays in your VPC; we can optionally deploy a fully air-gapped package where none of the traces leave. We'll capture the config options in the follow-up doc.
[05:36] Lina: For the pilot, what's the easiest path to reproduce an error and get you access to traces?
[05:43] Arjun: We can give you a short-lived support token that grants read-only access to the traces for demo time. Alternatively, you can export the trace JSON and upload to us. For debugging, it's often best to run a synthetic run with your traffic profile and we ingest the request ids.
[06:00] Ben: Is there a way to link user identity to traces without exposing PII? we do pseudonymous ids.
[06:07] Arjun: Yes, use hashed user ids or pass a correlation id. console will display the correlation id instead of full user fields if you mask them.
[06:15] Samir: On the infra side, curious about the routing policies — we sometimes want low-latency for a VIP subset and lower-cost for bulk processing. how are requests routed?
[06:26] Arjun: We have policy-based routing: route by latency SLO tier, cost tier, model variant, or region. you can set fallbacks and automatic snapshotting of model variants. We also have smart routing that routes to quantized variants when latency budgets are tight.
[06:44] Lina: Does the trace show quantization decisions?
[06:47] Arjun: Yes — trace lanes include kernel selection and quantization profile used for that invocation. sometimes the ASR writes "quan-tize" weirdly in the transcript.
[06:58] (laughter)
[07:02] Maya: Quick question from the product: what's your timeline for pilot and success criteria?
[07:08] Lina: We want a 1-week pilot with our staging traffic, success is: reproduce known 500s, reduce mean tail latency by 20% on those flows, and confirm logs are retained per our policy.
[07:20] Maya: Great. we'll propose a pilot plan — sample traces, dedicated sizing if needed, and a checklist for compliance.
[07:28] Ben: Any blockers on integration complexity? we run k8s on-prem with a VPN to cloud services.
[07:35] Arjun: For Private there's a straightforward operator and our on-prem package supports the core data plane components. for VPN + VPC peering we have docs and a partner network to help. Samir, you'll need to share network topology and we can map ports and firewall rules.
[07:51] Samir: ok i'll send that.
[07:55] Arjun: Also noted: some customers want request-level sampling to limit PHI exposure. console supports sampling policies and automatic redaction.
[08:08] Diane: We'll want to see retention and deletion controls for traces. is there a self-service deletion?
[08:15] Maya: Yes, retention policies per-tenant and self-service deletion APIs. We'll include the API docs.
[08:23] (screen - exporting logs)
[08:30] Arjun: Demo: export flow — choose time range, filter by model id or error, then export JSONL. you can click "include traces" which will bundle the trace JSONs.
[08:47] Ben: Nice. if we run a pilot and hit capacity, what happens?
[08:53] Maya: For Dedicated we have reserved capacity and burst options. for hosted we will auto-fall back to a compatible model variant if capacity constrained; that's visible on the trace and in the routing decision. we'll surface cost implications in the sizing doc.
[09:08] (transcript notes - minor ASR issues around proper nouns)
[09:15] Lina: ok last question: how long does it take to onboard and get the trial running?
[09:21] Maya: Typical pilot is 1-2 days to get sandboxed API keys and trace export configured, then run the weeklong benchmark. for Private or on-prem it can be 2-4 weeks depending on network approvals.
[09:36] Arjun: i'll follow up with a step-by-step pilot checklist.
[09:41] Maya: Cool, let's recap quick.
[09:44] Maya: Next steps: i'll send pricing and sizing, Arjun will send the runbook and sample traces, Samir will share traffic profile, Diane will confirm compliance items, and we'll target the week of 2026-08-17 for a pilot.
[10:02] Lina: Thanks everyone, that works.
[10:05] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links. Bye.

End of transcript.
